prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE finished, high-fidelity desktop website hero concept for OHMI, an electronics learning companion Chrome extension for college students. Landscape 1440x1000 composition, readable real typography and navigable website anatomy. Input 1 is the exact approved OHMI pixel-art mascot, preserve its exact design, silhouette, face, antennae, component details, original pixelated edges and proportions; use this as the hero subject, never a 3D reinterpretation. Input 2 is Nimbus mood/composition reference only: dark cinematic background, bold readable type, generous whitespace and a central friendly mascot, but adapt original OHMI branding and mint teal rather than blue. Premium graphic design, cohesive near-black green #071411 background, ivory #f5faf5 typography, mint #a0f0cd actions and accents. Self-hostable clean modern geometric sans character, heavy display but calm readable body. Navigation at top: small OHMI wordmark left, How it works and FAQ toward right, pill action 'Meet your buddy'. Exact main title: 'A little buddy.\nA brighter build.' Exact supporting copy: 'Meet OHMI, your learning companion for electronics, Arduino, and those why-isn’t-this-working moments.' Primary action 'Explore OHMI' and secondary 'See how it works'. Small honest source-build note 'Built for curious circuit builders.' No fake testimonials, numbers, store badges, verified-circuit claims or decorative data labels. This is a website comp with real text and controls, not a poster. No text boxes around every item. Show a narrow beginning of the next section at bottom to establish page continuation. Keep comfortable text contrast, sophisticated whitespace, nav and CTA fully visible, and mascot fully visible. CONCEPT B: 'Workbench'. A spacious asymmetric desktop layout. Headline and body fill left half, actions below; exact approved mint pixel-art mascot fills right half as a friendly oversized character, with restrained mint backlight and one fine orbital ellipse behind. Under the mascot a single shallow dark product-preview panel with readable chips 'Ask', 'Assignments', 'Guide' and 'Illustrative preview', plus question 'Why does an LED need a resistor?' and plain answer 'A resistor limits current and helps protect the LED.' Preserve a crisp tasteful product-site composition, no science-fiction HUD, no nested cards. Tiny circuit connection dots punctuate the dark backdrop, never cross the text. Lower edge shows the start of the open-layout heading 'Small questions. Real understanding.' This is a premium student product website, not an app dashboard.
